partnershipPlan: Two patient partners review the outcome definitions and the plain-language summary; a ward nurse from each service and an infection prevention nurse review the failure coding rule before extraction.
socialListening: No social media listening; patient complaints about cannulation from the two years are counted by month as context for the time series.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: By the fourth day I dreaded the morning round, because it meant another needle whether the old one worked or not.
items.implication: Report catheters per admission as a main secondary outcome.

items.theme: Fear of harm from longer dwell
items.quote: Composite paraphrase: I have seen arms swell up on day six, and nobody will convince me that leaving them in is harmless.
items.implication: Keep infiltration inside the failure definition and show failure by dwell day descriptively.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: At three in the morning with twelve patients, the phlebitis score is the first thing that gets skipped.
items.implication: Report documentation completeness by shift as a process measure.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: My mother could not tell anyone her arm hurt, and it was me who noticed the redness.
items.implication: Report failure for patients with delirium or limited English and state the limits of visual scoring.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: Two infections in a year is a signal to look, not a result; we would need years of data to see a real change.
items.implication: Report bloodstream infections as counts and do not test them.

summary: Five composite voices on insertions, fear of longer dwell, night assessment, recognising problems and reading rare infections.
